chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:

Indeed, Allah has made the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood) obligatory, and the recitation is a Sunnah. So whoever deliberately leaves the recitation, he must repeat the prayer, and whoever forgets the recitation, his prayer is complete and there is nothing upon him.
ai.seo_question: Does forgetting Quran recitation invalidate the Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic status of Quranic recitation (Qira'ah) in Salah, distinguishing between its obligatory nature in the first rak'ah and its recommended status in others, a nuance central to Shia fiqh. It establishes that deliberate omission invalidates the prayer requiring repetition, whereas unintentional forgetting does not, reflecting the principle of ease in worship. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual precision and divine mercy in Shia scholarly tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Allahazwj Necessitated the Rukū and the Sajdah, and the recitation is a Sunnah. So the one who neglects the recitation deliberately should repeat the Salāt, and the one who forgets the recitation, so he has completed his Salāt and there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i ibn ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ’

Allah has made Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) and Sujud (prostrations) obligatory. Recitation is Sunnah. Whoever omits recitation willfully performs Salah (prayer) again. Whoever forgets recitation his Salah (prayer) is complete and he is not obligated for anything in this matter.’”
